profile.description: GE Vernova designs, manufactures, delivers and services technologies for the electric power system, including gas turbines, wind turbines and grid equipment, selling to utilities, power producers, industrial and government customers worldwide.

segments.name: Power
segments.sells: Gas, steam, nuclear and related power generation equipment and services
segments.end_markets: Power generation, industrial, government and other customers worldwide, with demand from hyperscalers and data centers

segments.name: Wind
segments.sells: Onshore and offshore wind turbines and blades, and related services

segments.name: Electrification
segments.sells: Grid solutions, power conversion and storage, and electrification software for transmission, distribution, conversion and storage of electricity
segments.end_markets: Utilities, grid operators and industrial customers

geography.summary: Revenues are classified by region of sale. In 2025 the US was $17,341 million of $38,068 million total; non-US was $20,728 million (Europe $7,594M, Asia $4,629M, Middle East and Africa $5,389M, rest of Americas $3,116M).

evidence.quote: Revenues are classified according to the region to which equipment and services are sold.
presented separately from the remainder of the Americas.

customers.summary: Customers are power generators, utilities, industrial and government buyers; the Power segment cites hyperscaler and data center demand. No concentration figure found.

evidence.quote: Our Power segment serves power generation, industrial, government, and other customers worldwide with products and services
power to support industrialization, grid stability needs, and rising electricity demand from hyperscalers and data centers

backlog.latest: RPO of $150.2 billion at December 31, 2025 (vs $119.0 billion at December 31, 2024)
backlog.horizon: Equipment RPO ($64.2B): 37% within 1 year; Services RPO ($86.0B): 17% within 1 year (implies roughly 26% of total RPO, derived)
backlog.summary: RPO is the company's backlog measure; equipment RPO converts faster than long-dated service contracts.

pricing.summary: Pricing and contract terms are adjusted for demand, inflation and industry dynamics; favorable price was a named driver of 2025 revenue and EBITDA growth in Power and Electrification. Tariffs are mitigated through supply chain and US manufacturing moves.

evidence.quote: We adjust pricing and contractual terms of our products and services based on demand, inflation, and industry dynamics.
Segment EBITDA increased $0.7 billion organically*, primarily due to volume, favorable price, and productivity at Grid Solutions.
mitigate the impact of tariffs, we are diversifying our supply chains, increasing U.S. manufacturing capabilities, and engaging with policy

margin_drivers.summary: Favorable price, volume and productivity drove segment EBITDA gains in Power (Gas and Steam) and Electrification (Grid Solutions), partly offset by investment expenses and inflation; Offshore Wind remains pressured by project costs and execution timelines.

Load growth raises the need for generation and grid capacity.
